title: Improve notes formatting, comparison, and mTool review workflows

body:
## Summary

Fixes the eight findings from the Windows agent-trace audit of runs 183-185 (AMSB, Nielsen, VM), plus three human-file comparison display problems found while reviewing run 185.

**Extraction and notes**
- **Share classes (wrong capital figures):** Issued Capital must list every disclosed share class (for example preference shares in a separate note) before finishing. A missing or stale list leaves the sheet flagged on every successful exit, including timeout recovery.
- **Appearance checker:** tables are reviewed one at a time with their heading and year line. A structure finding must quote text from that table, and evidence that is rejected or describes a content defect never triggers a table re-copy.
- **Continued tables and emphasis:** refusals now say "needs source correction", naming the pages and any doubt recorded during preparation. Bold or underline copied from the source, which the formatter cannot remove, is reported instead of retried.
- **Cross-sheet write hint:** the hint now follows current vs non-current, and a successful write to the suggested cell clears the earlier rejection.
- **Mandatory fields:** feedback offers the audited "not disclosed" path instead of inviting invented zeros, and the first acknowledgement after verification is accepted.
- **Review routing (reverses an earlier decision):** a failed notes↔face tie-out no longer suppresses the figures triage that a clean run receives. The tie-out itself stays failed.
- **Cleanup:** a rejection lists every unsafe removal with its cell, block and page. The prompt no longer claims notes are already formatted.

**Human-file comparison**
- Calculated totals that appear twice on a sheet (SOCI "Total comprehensive income", SOCF cash at end of period) are derived from the human file's inputs instead of showing blank. Scores are unchanged.
- Stacked worksheet navigation on narrow windows scrolls away instead of covering the figures.
- Empty mTool spacer columns no longer force human note tables into an 840px scrolling region, and figures and headings no longer split mid-word.

Not included: automatic repair of source content or emphasis (needs a product decision), and sending statements finished with an acknowledged flag into figures triage.

## Test plan

body:
Extraction could discard an issued save at its node cap, or preserve a timed-out workbook while reporting unflagged success without current verification or accepted source coverage. Preparation could also accept table evidence that was absent from the submitted candidate. These paths now preserve bounded completion work and retain incomplete/source-defect outcomes for review.

Changes:
- Allow one issued tool node to finish at the iteration cap under the existing timeout. Preserve terminal output and committed saves without starting another model request; tool-turn and token limits remain enforced.
- Flag salvaged work when verification is absent/negative or face coverage remains unaccounted. Carry the flag through the completion event so the parent run reports errors while retaining written figures.
- Bind positive table-verification receipts to exact current candidate cell coordinates/text, including coverage of each nested table. Reject invalid claims through bounded repair and best-effort uncertainty. Advance the preparation contract version so older approvals are not reused.
- Replace the impossible missing-policy `save_result` instruction with a grounded reporting tool. Persist the exact live field's reason/pages/evidence as a human-review flag and include it in the reviewer packet; the mandatory field remains unresolved.
- Keep source-content, wrong-page, emphasis-removal and geometry defects out of the style-correction loop. Explicitly reject unsupported emphasis removal instead of silently ignoring it. Source emphasis/content guards remain intact; these defects require human/source correction.

The original Windows page-swap cause is still unknown. Candidate evidence binding does not replace independent source judgment or guarantee that a model can never misread the PDF. This PR does not attempt historical cost optimization or relax mandatory applicability rules.

Depends on #29 and targets `fix/page-transcript-compaction` so its already-implemented page-retention fix is reviewed separately. Merge #29 first, then retarget this PR to `main`.

Validation:

- Remaining applicable model/transport, loop, persistence and source-integrity pinning checks: 405 passed.

- Full backend suite (`venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/ -n auto -q --tb=short`): 6,217 passed, 34 skipped, 2 failed. Two existing native Group fixture cases fail at fixture lookup (`StopIteration`, before application calls) because `data/*Group_SOFP*.xlsx` and `data/*Group_FirstTime*.xlsx` are absent. A serial run of the unchanged mTool test file reproduces those two failures; 19 other tests pass and two are skipped.

Native Windows execution and exact Windows receipt replay were unavailable. Live/paid model runs were not performed. Frontend builds/tests and template/taxonomy generation are not applicable to this backend/prompt-only change.
title: Fix extraction completion and source-verification failure handling

body:
## Problem
Notes formatting runs one agent per sheet (or per table group on large sheets), but Activity showed one flat list of identical "Checking formatted notes against the source PDF…" lines with no way to tell sections apart.

## Change
- `notes/formatter_activity.py`: each formatter pass reports started / working / finished-or-failed status and its tool calls. Tools report themselves, so model requests keep their non-streaming transport.
- Live: events stream under `agent_id="notes-formatting"` with `sub_agent_id` (= the pass's `run_agents.variant`).
- Saved: events are written on the pass's own `run_agents` row with the time each event happened (`log_event` gains an optional `ts`).
- A pass cancelled at its deadline is recorded as a time-limit failure; an earlier cancellation stays "stopped".
- UI: the live Notes formatting tab and History show sub-agent tabs (shared `FormatterSubAgentActivity`); "All" names each sub-agent on its lines; only failures are marked. Runs saved before this change keep the existing view.

body:
## Problem
Run 179 (Nielsen SOFP) hit its 60-step limit after 28 page-reading calls (217 pages requested across 26 distinct pages). Totals balanced; the agent ran out of steps before submitting.

Text compaction kept only the newest `read_page_text` result **per tool name**, so reading pages 25–33 replaced the pages 16–24 transcript with a placeholder, and the agent re-read both batches in a loop. Aggressive compaction was also on almost all the time: the 60,000 watermark counted the running total of re-sent tokens, which every healthy SOFP run passed by its third request.

## Change
- Page transcripts are compacted only after a later read covers all their pages; the placeholder names the pages.
- The soft watermark measures the current request size (latest model response usage). Default 60,000 → 100,000; healthy SOFP requests peaked at 49k–67k in five local traces.

## Checks
- New/updated tests in `tests/test_history_processor_escalation.py` (4 fail on the old code).
- Full backend suite: all pass except 2 `test_mtool_filing_resolution` failures that also fail on `main`.
- Not run: a live extraction. Before merging, rerun SOFP on Nielsen; on Windows, clear any saved `XBRL_SOFT_COMPACT_TOKENS=60000` setting (it would now apply to the current request size).

## What this does

Makes notes formatting more reliable, and fixes three problems found in review.

**Formatting (branch `claude/notes-formatting-hardening`)**
- The formatter describes each table's structure; code turns that into the actual formatting, instead of the model writing styles directly.
- Fixes rule-line placement seen in live runs and adds boxed tables.
- A table copied wrongly from the PDF is now re-copied from the source page instead of only being flagged. One re-copy can fix every table on that page with the same defect, and recorded page-banner removals are replayed onto the rebuilt note (schema v52).
- Only a table's leading heading rows get heading styling.

**Review fixes (4a62810)**
1. **Person ownership:** the formatter now re-checks inside its final save that no person has taken over a note. Before, someone saving identical text during a formatting pass lost ownership of that note.
2. **Simultaneous corrections:** each prepared document now has a lock covering the whole read-modify-write. Before, two simultaneous table corrections could leave only one saved on disk.
3. **Partial results:** a model failure during table re-copy, or during the formatting pass after it, now stays on the affected row. Before, it also discarded rows already saved, their counts and their verification receipts.
4. Removed trailing whitespace flagged by `git diff --check`.

Numeric merge identity now includes taxonomy dimensions, so ordinary and preference shares remain separate while a later reading of the same class replaces its earlier value. Saved Activity now combines preparation progress and notes formatting, cleanup, and completeness stages with the workstream event feeds. Preparation workers persist their attempt identity, so retries starting in the same second retain their own activity. The reused document-map worker matches its latest attempt; a later remap does not inherit an earlier attempt's updates. Historical workers without a starting event retain timestamp matching only when the timestamps distinguish attempts. title: Finalize automatic notes review and content-bound verification

body:
PDF notes can retain their text and numbers while formatting places a border on the wrong row or misses a comparative-year rule. This change checks each prepared output table against the source PDF before saving formatting, with one bounded style correction and recheck.

### Behavior

- Use a fresh checker context containing the prepared HTML used by review and Copy, table geometry, and all known source pages. Missing, duplicate, unexpected, or unsupported table assessments remain unresolved, including no-op formatting proposals.
- Give the initial check and recheck a separate shared allowance of eight requests. Formatting and correction retain the existing configurable allowance, defaulting to sixteen requests. Preserve unrelated passed rows when later correction or rechecking exhausts its allowance, and aggregate both roles' usage.
- Keep content, numbers, and table geometry unchanged. Retain atomic compare-and-swap writes and revert snapshots for saved rows only. Preserve original findings and log rejected corrections.
- Surface checking, correction, and rechecking in automatic pipeline events and manual formatter status. Retain visual evidence in grouped results and add the checker prompt to the generated audit.
- Share direct table-row coordinates between geometry, patch targeting, and verification. Detect malformed row nesting during preparation and reject attempts to certify it with style-only patches; advance the preparation contract to invalidate older cached assessments.

Separate commits restore live destinations for unresolved parent notes without clearing their review status, and fix PDF zoom width and horizontal-scroll reset on Fit to width.

This PR retains post-review notes formatting. Moving source-formatting recognition into document preparation is a separate proposed redesign. The checker reads prepared HTML and source images; it does not certify native Word or mTool rendering.

The three workstreams are separated into commits:
- `6ab6ddf`: PDF table verification checks source/candidate relationships, permits source-confirmed blank-padded section headings, and preserves every capture/check receipt in content-addressed audit files referenced by the checkpoint. Table verdict and provider-error classification logic is shared. Negative table verdicts remain unresolved, including when candidate HTML has no table, to protect against omitted source tables.
- `5b1d35b`: Notes appearance and 0.75px mTool/clipboard border defaults, with synchronized settings, editor actions, output preparation, documentation, and tests. Canonical double-border intent remains available in the editor; prepared output uses single lines.
- `2ffa3a3`: The formatter supports canonical text disclosures on numeric notes sheets. Shared identity validation and a repository bulk lookup exclude numeric, mismatched, or quarantined targets and revalidate eligibility before saving.

## Problem

The per-row SOCF sign-convention block (`prompts/_sign_conventions.py`) reads each `*Total …` formula's `+1`/`-1` coefficient correctly, but its **prose guidance** only covered:

- the gain/loss case for **ADDED** rows, and
- the payment case for **SUBTRACTED** rows.

An agent therefore pattern-matched the SUBTRACTED *"Cash payments → enter positive magnitude"* example onto **ADDED** outflow rows — e.g. row 109 `Cash payments for the principal portion of the lease liability` (`+1*B109`) — and entered `+3,732` instead of `-3,732` (the documented Amway discrepancy). Because the `*Total` formula adds an ADDED cell as-is (no sign flip), a positive value wrongly **inflates** the section subtotal.

This is the inconsistency the user hit: some outflows are subtracted (`Repayments of borrowings`, enter positive) while others are added (lease principal/interest payments, `Repurchase of treasury shares`, sukuk issuance expenses, etc., which must be entered **negative**).

## Fix

Prompt-guidance only — **no template formula edits** (gotcha #3; formulas trace to the SSM linkbase). Extended the ADDED branch to spell out three cases explicitly:

- ADDED **outflow** (payment/repayment/purchase/repurchase/acquisition/deposit placed/…paid/issuance expenses) → enter **NEGATIVE**, with worked `-3,732` lease example.
- ADDED **inflow** (Proceeds/Receipts/Withdrawal/…received) → positive.
- ADDED gain/loss → directional (loss positive, gain negative), as before.

Plus a contrast note: the same "Cash payments" wording flips entry sign depending on whether *this* template's formula adds or subtracts that row — obey the per-row ADDED/SUBTRACTED label, not the row name alone.

## Tests

- New `test_added_outflow_rows_get_negative_entry_guidance` pins the NEGATIVE instruction, the worked example, and the ADDED/SUBTRACTED-label warning.
- `python3 -m pytest tests/test_socf_sign_convention.py -q` → **9 passed**.

- **Phase 1** — cache read/write telemetry end-to-end → schema **v15** (`cache_read_tokens` / `cache_write_tokens` on `run_agents` + `run_agent_turns`). Auto-migrates on startup; existing rows backfill to 0.
- **Phase 2** — provider-correct prompt caching via `model_settings.build_model_settings` (Anthropic cache breakpoints; OpenAI `prompt_cache_key` + 24h retention; provider gating so a proxy-routed Gemini/Claude doesn't get OpenAI-only params).
- **Phase 3** — **trimmed on a live measurement**: `gpt-5.4` run showed **76.6% cross-turn cache-hit rate**, so the speculative follow-ups were dropped and the dormant `cache_template` flag deleted. `scripts/cache_report.py` reads the metrics from the DB without the web UI.

## Track B — Effectiveness (built + test-pinned; quality gain NOT yet measured)
- **Phase 4** — pre-inject cascade traces into the reviewer packet.
- **Phase 5** — resolve notes-prompt contradictions (one-sheet invariant; catch-all vs skip).
- **Phase 6** — de-hardcode SOCIE movement rows (read from `read_template()`); single-source the sign-convention block.
- **Phase 7** — directional sign-error diagnostics for non-SOFP verifiers (no-plug guard preserved); "verify is near-vacuous off SOFP" warning.
- **Phase 8** — confidence-gate scanned-PDF scout refs; `save_infopack` survival counts.
- **Phase 9** — provider-aware temperature (Gemini + OpenAI-reasoning stay 1.0; others lowered).
- **Phase 10** — magnitude-scaled SOFP balance tolerance.

Plus 3 peer-review rounds (provider gating, notes cache rollup, a non-dict inventory crash, a SOCIE cross-check wording fix, a workbook-handle close, stale-comment cleanup).

## Honest evaluation caveat
Across N runs on the FYE-2022 PDF, the **caching track is proven** (76.6% hit rate) but the **effectiveness track shows no measurable quality gain yet** — the one post-change run sits inside the normal before-run variance (dominated by temperature-1.0 non-determinism). A real verdict on Phases 4–10 needs multiple after-runs **and** value-level accuracy scoring against the actual figures (internal reconciliation ≠ correct numbers). Each effectiveness change does target a real, test-pinned failure mode.

## Windows / proxy testing notes
- DB auto-migrates to v15 on first startup.
- Two Windows-relevant hardening fixes included: `_sign_conventions.py` workbook close (gotcha #22) and the scout non-dict-inventory crash guard.
- The key untestable-here question this unblocks: does a **proxy-routed** run still get cache reads on the enterprise proxy (Step 2.2)?

## Tests
Full backend suite **1904 passed / 2 skipped**. Every behavior-changing phase updates its pinning test in the same commit.

## Summary

Hardening follow-ups from a five-axis review of the reviewer-agent feature (`2403177`), plus the loopback-bind portion of the spun-off auth task. No feature changes — all surgical fixes with pinning tests.

## Changes

**Reviewer backend hardening** (`31533b4`)
- Template-family-scope the reviewer write path (`apply_reviewer_fix`) — refuse an off-family `concept_uuid` so a hallucinated id can't write an unrenderable fact row (gotcha #21).
- Scrub raw exception text from the four reviewer error paths (snapshot / construction / run / background thread) — stable codes + generic messages, full trace logged server-side only (LLM-SDK errors can embed the bearer token; mirrors `/test-connection`).
- Close the `_REVIEW_TASKS` re-entrancy TOCTOU with a lock.
- Make `revert_to_original` atomic (snapshot-exists check inside `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`) and return a `recomputed` flag instead of propagating a post-restore cascade failure.
- Cap concurrent reviewer passes with a `BoundedSemaphore` (`XBRL_MAX_CONCURRENT_REVIEWS`, default 3) → 429 when saturated; bound the in-process registry.
- Validate the re-review model override (length cap → 422, unknown id → soft warn) and guidance length; cap `human_answer` at 8000 chars.

**Reviewer UI** (`219e806`)
- The Review tab now surfaces the server's `detail` instead of a bare `HTTP 422`, so the new caps / 429 / 409 messages render in the error banner.

**Network exposure** (`78410f1`, `c54a3d8`)
- Default uvicorn bind to `127.0.0.1` (was `0.0.0.0`); `HOST=0.0.0.0` is an explicit opt-in that logs a warning. The app has no auth/CORS/CSRF but exposes destructive + paid-LLM endpoints, so all-interfaces was unsafe by default.
- `.env.example` template defaulted to loopback so fresh clones don't re-introduce the exposure.

## Tests
- New: `tests/test_bind_host_default.py` (4), plus 3 template-scope write tests in `tests/test_reviewer_tools.py`.
- Reviewer suites green; lifecycle + bind tests green.

## Out of scope (future work)
The full bearer-token auth + CORS allow-list for multi-host deployments. Loopback default neutralizes the practical risk for local single-user use.
